# fenced-code-language

- ID: `MD040`
- Category: Code
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `code`, `language`

Fenced code blocks name their language after the opening fence.

## Why

Renderers use the language to highlight the code.

## Options

Set them under `rules.fenced-code-language.options`.

- `allowed_languages` (`string[]`, default `[]`): Languages to allow. An empty
  list allows every language.
- `language_only` (`boolean`, default `false`): Report an info string that holds
  more than the language.

## Fix

The fix adds a language only when gomdlint can detect it with certainty, such as
from a shebang line or valid JSON, and when allowed\_languages, if set, names it
exactly. gomdlint reports every other finding without a fix. gomdlint may report
a finding without a fix when the fix would change a line with one character in
brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line,
because it could add or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

````markdown
# Scripts

```
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "gomdlint lint docs"
  }
}
```
````

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 Fenced code block has no language specified
```

The fix changes it to:

````markdown
# Scripts

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "gomdlint lint docs"
  }
}
```
````

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  fenced-code-language:
    options:
      allowed_languages: []
```

Under `rules`, `fenced-code-language: false` turns the rule off and
`fenced-code-language: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable fenced-code-language` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line fenced-code-language -->
```
